description: Trigger and behavior cases for LLM output handling: untrusted output to render/execute/URL/tool/store sinks, context-correct encoding, generated-code sandboxing, the generated-code commit path (LLM10:2026), second-order injection, exploit-flow-gated severity.

cases.prompt: Review our AI feature's output handling: the model's answer is rendered as markdown in the dashboard, and a separate 'run this query' mode executes the SQL it generates.

assertions: Treats model output as untrusted and enumerates the render (markdown) and execute (SQL) sinks.
Flags raw-HTML-in-markdown as XSS unless sanitized with an allowlist, and requires parameterization/allowlisting for the generated SQL.
Names the output→sink→impact flow per finding and gates severity on a concrete exploit.
Recommends CSP/defense-in-depth without treating it as a substitute for encoding.

cases.prompt: Our data agent writes Python and we exec() it on the server to compute the answer. It has the DB credentials in the environment. Is this safe?

assertions: Identifies unsandboxed generated-code execution as RCE-class and a blocking finding.
Requires a real sandbox: isolation, no ambient credentials, network denied/allowlisted, resource limits — not prompt-level 'write safe code' assurances.
Routes remediation of the credential-exposed exec path through human-approval-boundary.

cases.prompt: Define the JSON schema our model must return and reject responses that don't match the required fields and types.

assertions: Schema-shape validation of structured output is structured-output-validator; this skill reviews injection/execution sinks, and shape-valid output can still be an unsafe value.

cases.prompt: We store the model's output as internal data, so when the admin console later renders it we skip escaping since it's from our own system. Confirm that's fine.

assertions: Rejects the assumption: stored model output is untrusted again on read (second-order), and the admin console rendering it raw is an XSS sink.
Requires context-correct encoding at the sink that uses the data, not a trust assumption because it's 'internal'.
Explains that model output is attacker-influenced whenever untrusted content was in context.

cases.prompt: Stop attackers from manipulating what our model produces by hiding instructions in the documents it reads.

assertions: llm-output-safety-reviewer does not activate: preventing hidden instructions from manipulating the model is the input-side injection defense; this skill assumes output is adversarial and secures its consuming sinks.
Does not auto-invoke prompt-injection-defender (MANUAL-ONLY); may name it and recommend explicit invocation, and does not silently substitute llm-output-safety-reviewer for it.

cases.prompt: Our coding assistant writes code straight into the working tree and a bot commits it to a feature branch. Review how we handle that AI-generated code before it is committed and run.

assertions: Treats the generated code as untrusted model output and reviews the save/commit/run path as a sink (LLM10:2026, insecure generated code).
Checks that nothing auto-executes the code and that any pre-review run happens in a sandbox with no ambient credentials.
Requires static checks (tests, linters, SAST, secret scan) before a human review gate that the author or bot cannot bypass, plus a provenance label marking the change as AI-generated.
Routes any dependency the generated code adds to supply-chain-security-reviewer and leaves the line-by-line diff review to code-reviewer or security-pr-reviewer rather than performing it itself.

cases.prompt: The agent only writes files, it never runs anything. It just added a new .github/workflows file and a postinstall script to package.json. We review everything at PR time. Anything to worry about?

assertions: Rejects 'it only writes files': a generated CI workflow or install script executes on the next push or install, possibly before any reviewer sees it, so those paths are execution sinks.
Requires that generated content in auto-executing paths is held for human review before it can run, and that CI for unreviewed branches cannot reach secrets.
Routes the CI-workflow and install-script supply-chain review itself to supply-chain-security-reviewer rather than re-performing it.

cases.prompt: Our AI agent writes the fix, writes the tests, the tests pass and the SAST scan is green, so we let it merge its own PR to main, which auto-deploys. Confirm that's an adequate gate for generated code.

assertions: Refuses to confirm: an agent that commits and merges its own generated code to a deploying branch with no human review gate is a blocking finding.
Explains that a green scan and tests written by the same model are evidence for a human reviewer, not approval.
Routes remediation through human-approval-boundary.

Does not redesign standing merge authority itself: names agent-authorization-matrix (MANUAL-ONLY, recommend explicit invocation, never auto-invoked) or ai-sdlc-operating-model as the owner of who may merge.
